body.zh-Hant: 據《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》，埃利奧多羅·比利亞松出身玻利維亞科恰班巴省的薩卡巴，受過法律訓練，1871年當選科恰班巴代表進入議會，當時年僅二十三歲。該條目記其生卒為1848年1月22日至1940年9月14日；德國國家圖書館權威檔則記出生地為薩卡巴、卒地為科恰班巴，生卒年為1849與1939，兩者年份不一致。
body.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture, Eliodoro Villazón was born in Sacaba in the department of Cochabamba and trained as a lawyer; he became deputy from Cochabamba to the Assembly of 1871 when he was only twenty-three. That entry gives his dates as 22 January 1848 to 14 September 1940, while the German National Library authority file records Sacaba as birthplace and Cochabamba as place of death, with years 1849 and 1939; the two sources disagree on the years.

heading.zh-Hant: 財政部長、自由黨與外交部長
heading.en: Finance minister, Liberal Party and foreign minister

body.zh-Hant: 據同一條目，比利亞松在1880年國民大會上引起剛上任的總統納西索·坎佩羅（任期1880至1884年）的注意，在坎佩羅政府下被任命為財政部長，後來擔任駐歐洲財政代理人。返國後他加入自由黨，成為最忠誠的黨員之一；1898年聯邦戰爭後自由黨上台，他出任外交部長。
body.en: The same entry says that at the National Convention of 1880 Villazón caught the attention of Narciso Campero, the recently installed president (1880–1884). Under Campero he was appointed minister of finance and later financial agent in Europe. After returning from abroad he joined the Liberal Party and became one of its most loyal members. When the Liberals came to power after the Federal War of 1898, he became minister of foreign affairs.

body.zh-Hant: 據該條目，自由黨領袖伊斯馬埃爾·蒙特斯（1904至1908年任總統）挑選比利亞松為黨的總統候選人，因蒙特斯的繼任者去世而必須舉行特別選舉，比利亞松以壓倒性票數當選，扮演為蒙特斯看守的角色。任內他持續政府對鐵路建設的支持，並成功與歐洲人談妥貸款，促成國家銀行（Banco de la Nación）的成立。德國國家圖書館權威檔則記他為1909至1913年的玻利維亞總統。
body.en: According to the entry, Ismael Montes, leader of the Liberals and president from 1904 to 1908, selected Villazón as the party's presidential candidate in a special election made necessary by the death of Montes's successor. Elected overwhelmingly, Villazón, as caretaker for Montes, continued government support for railroad construction and successfully negotiated loans with Europeans that led to the formation of the Banco de la Nación. The German National Library authority file records him as president of Bolivia 1909–1913.

heading.en: Origins, studies and brief civil service

body.zh-Hant: 據《奧地利傳記辭典》，米夏埃爾·海尼施1858年8月15日生於下奧地利的奧厄，曾就讀萊比錫大學與維也納大學，1882年取得法學博士，之後短暫在法院、財政檢察署與教育部任職（1886至1890年）。據《新德意志傳記》，他把學術興趣放在前面，物質上的獨立使他在四年後就離開了公職。
body.en: According to the Österreichisches Biographisches Lexikon, Michael Hainisch was born at Aue near Schottwien on 15 August 1858, studied at the universities of Leipzig and Vienna, and took his doctorate in law in 1882. After a short spell at a court, in the Finanzprokuratur and in the Ministry of Education (1886–1890) he left. The Neue Deutsche Biographie adds that he put his scholarly interests first and that his material independence let him leave the civil service after four years.

citations.quote: Aue b. Schottwien (N.Ö.), 15. 8. 1858
Stud. am Akadem. Gymn. und an den Univ. Leipzig und Wien, 1882 Dr.jur.
Nach kurzer Tätigkeit bei Gericht
in der Finanzprokuratur und im Unterrichtsmin. (1886–90)
da er seine wissenschaftlichen Interessen in den Vordergrund stellte
ermöglichte ihm schon nach vier Jahren den Austritt

body.zh-Hant: 據《奧地利傳記辭典》，海尼施1889年組織民眾教育協會，並成為中央圖書館的共同創辦人；他屬於奧地利的「費邊社」，1898年參加布魯塞爾國際勞工保護大會，當時也被聘入商務部勞工統計局顧問會。1916年他在柏林發表批評匈牙利糧食供應態度的言論，受到外交部長切爾寧的訓斥；1918年他以德奧儲蓄銀行代表身分進入奧匈銀行總務委員會。
body.en: According to the ÖBL, Hainisch organised adult-education societies in 1889 and became a co-founder of the Zentralbibliothek; he was among Austria's "Fabians", took part in the International Labour Protection Congress in Brussels in 1898 and was then also called to the advisory council of the Labour Statistics Office in the Commerce Ministry. A criticism he delivered in Berlin in 1916 of Hungary's conduct in food supply earned him a reprimand from Foreign Minister Czernin; in 1918, as representative of the German-Austrian savings banks, he entered the general council of the Austro-Hungarian Bank.

citations.quote: H. organisierte 1889 Volksbildungsver. und wurde Mitbegründer der Zentralbibl.
So war er bei den österr. „Fabiern“ zu finden
nahm am Internat. Arbeiterschutzkongreß Brüssel 1898 teil

Als Vertreter der dt.- österr. Sparkassen
kam H. noch 1918 in den Generalrat der Österr.-Ung. Bank

body.zh-Hant: 據《奧地利傳記辭典》，1920年12月9日聯邦大會在資產階級執政黨的妥協下選出海尼施為第一任聯邦總統；1924年再度當選，1928年卸任。據《新德意志傳記》，第一部聯邦憲法只給國家元首象徵性的角色；1921年他個人參與了與捷克斯洛伐克簽訂拉納條約的籌備，因而遭到德意志民族派的強烈攻擊。
body.en: According to the ÖBL, on 9 December 1920, on the basis of a compromise between the bourgeois governing parties, the Federal Assembly elected Hainisch the first Federal President; he was re-elected in 1924 and withdrew in 1928. The NDB says the first federal constitution gave the head of state only a representative role, and that in 1921 he personally took part in preparing the Treaty of Lana with Czechoslovakia, which exposed him to sharp polemic from the German-national side.

citations.quote: am 9. 12. 1920 auf Grund eines Kompromisses
die Wahl zum ersten Bundespräs. durch die Bundesversmlg. auf H.
1924 erfolgte seine Wiederwahl
1928 zog sich H. von seiner hohen Stellung

body.zh-Hant: 據《新德意志傳記》，海尼施卸任總統後回到學術工作，1929年被召入舒伯政府任商務部長。因他在各政黨中沒有後盾，一開始就遇到阻力；他於1930年6月16日提前辭職，理由是與匈牙利、南斯拉夫的商約談判會嚴重損害工業。《奧地利傳記辭典》記他獲維也納科學院榮譽院士，並獲多所大學授予名譽博士。
body.en: According to the NDB, after his presidency Hainisch returned to scholarly work and in 1929 was called into the Schober government as trade minister. Having no backing in the parties, he met difficulties from the start; he resigned early on 16 June 1930 because he believed that the trade-treaty negotiations with Hungary and Yugoslavia would seriously harm industry. The ÖBL records that he was an honorary member of the Academy of Sciences in Vienna and held honorary doctorates from several universities.

body.zh-Hant: 據《西班牙語文學虛擬圖書館》，阿爾弗雷多·薩亞斯1861年生於哈瓦那，出身靠製糖業致富的貴族家庭，受過良好教育並取得法學學位。他的父親與兄長積極參與反對宗主國的獨立運動，他本人被逮捕審判後遭流放西班牙，1895至1898年待在馬德里。《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》稱他是反抗西班牙統治鬥爭中的城市領袖，生於1861年9月21日。
body.en: According to the Biblioteca Virtual de la Filología Española, Alfredo Zayas was born in Havana in 1861 into an aristocratic family enriched by the sugar industry, was carefully educated and took a law degree. His father and brother were active in the independence struggle against the metropolis; he himself was arrested, tried, convicted and deported to Madrid, where he stayed from 1895 to 1898. The Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture calls him an urban leader of the struggle against Spanish domination and gives his birth as 21 September 1861.

citations.quote: Vio la luz en La Habana, en 1861
familia aristocrática enriquecida por los réditos de la industria azucarera
recibió una educación esmerada, que culminó con una licenciatura de Derecho
fueron unos activos militantes en la lucha contra la metrópoli
fue condenado y deportado a la España peninsular para cumplir condena en Madrid
donde permaneció entre 1895 y 1898
An urban leader of the struggle against Spanish domination
b. 21 September 1861; d. 11 April 1934

heading.zh-Hant: 共和國初期公職與副總統
heading.en: Early republican offices and vice presidency

body.zh-Hant: 據《西班牙語文學虛擬圖書館》，薩亞斯1901年是起草古巴憲法的制憲會議代表，1902至1906年任參議員，1906至1909年任哈瓦那市議員、檢察官與法官，並任副總統（該來源記1908至1913年）。《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》則記他1905年任參議院議長、1906年為革命領袖，並在第二次美國干預期間（1906至1909年）擔任占領當局的顧問，1909至1913年任副總統；兩來源對副總統起年不同。
body.en: According to the BVFE, Zayas was a delegate to the 1901 convention that drafted the Cuban constitution, senator from 1902 to 1906, councillor, prosecutor and judge of Havana from 1906 to 1909, and vice president of the Republic (that source: 1908–1913). The Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture records him as president of the Senate in 1905, revolutionary leader in 1906, adviser to the occupation authorities during the second U.S. intervention (1906–1909), and vice president in 1909–1913; the two sources differ on the start year of the vice presidency.

citations.quote: delegado de la convención que redactó el texto constitucional cubano en 1901
senador entre 1902 y 1906
concejal, fiscal y juez de La Habana entre 1906 y 1909
vicepresidente de la República entre 1908 y 1913
president of the Senate (1905)
revolutionary leader (1906)
the second U.S. intervention in Cuba (1906–1909)
In 1909–1913 he was vice president

body.zh-Hant: 據《西班牙語文學虛擬圖書館》，1916年薩亞斯參選總統但落敗，並受到保守派對手的迫害；1921年他領導自由黨，終於取得總統職位，任期到1925年。《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》同樣寫他在1921年終於登上總統之位。
body.en: According to the BVFE, Zayas ran for the presidency in 1916 but was defeated and persecuted by his conservative adversaries; in 1921, heading the Liberal Party, he reached the presidency, which he held until 1925. The Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture likewise says that in 1921 he finally succeeded in ascending to the presidency.

citations.quote: En 1916 se presentó como candidato a la presidencia del país
pero fue derrotado y perseguido por sus adversarios conservadores
en 1921 y encabezando al Partido Liberal, alcanzó la presidencia
la presidencia, que ostentó hasta 1925
in 1921 finally succeeded in ascending to the presidency

body.zh-Hant: 據《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》，薩亞斯政府的任期以裙帶、貪污著稱，但他重建了古巴因糖業危機受損的國際信用，並設法限制美國特使克勞德將軍的干預，1925年取得松樹島的主權。任內他要面對哈瓦那大學學潮、多次罷工以及退伍軍人與愛國者協會的起事，但偏好妥協而非暴力。1925年他未能爭取連任，將總統職位交給赫拉多·馬查多將軍，退居私人生活。
body.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture, Zayas's administration was marked by nepotism, graft and corruption, yet he reestablished Cuba's international credit, which had suffered from a sugar crisis, kept the interference of U.S. envoy General Enoch Crowder within certain bounds, and secured title to the Isle of Pines in 1925. In office he faced student turbulence at the University of Havana, numerous strikes and an uprising organized by the Veterans' and Patriots' Association, but preferred compromise to violence. In 1925, unable to secure his own reelection, he ceded the presidency to General Gerardo Machado y Morales and retired to private life.

which had been suffering from a sugar crisis

body.zh-Hant: 據《西班牙語文學虛擬圖書館》，薩亞斯是業餘詞典學者，著有兩卷本《安的列斯詞彙學》（哈瓦那，1914年），收錄源自島上原住民語言的西班牙語詞彙並說明詞源與語義，其第二版於1931年出版。他退出政治後轉向學術工作，1934年以73歲在出生地哈瓦那自然死亡。《拉丁美洲歷史與文化百科全書》記他卒於1934年4月11日。
body.en: According to the BVFE, Zayas was an amateur lexicographer whose major work was the two-volume Lexicografía antillana (Havana, 1914), recording Spanish words derived from the aboriginal languages of the islands with etymology and meaning; a second edition appeared in 1931. Retired from political battle, he returned to scholarly tasks and in 1934, aged 73, died of natural causes in his native city. The Encyclopedia of Latin American History and Culture gives his death as 11 April 1934.
